analysis: The PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/model-registry.md, docs/developer/build.md and docs/developer/test.md. None of these edits changes runtime behavior, keys, attestation, authorization, encryption, billing, or the TB-002/TB-011 gates. The model-registry.md change (head lines 17-22) documents a ModelMediaPolicy.advertisesMedia guard that keeps staged nemotron_h_omni checkpoints from advertising media support. It states that the guard does not enable text inference, qualify a RAM tier, or register the model. This is conservative and consistent with the registry's fail-closed capability advertisement. I did not see ModelMediaPolicy.swift, so the guard's implementation is not reviewed. A later pass should confirm the code matches the doc: the architecture match is case- and whitespace-insensitive, and it applies regardless of HF repo ID or alias. The build.md and test.md additions (Nemotron Super component qualification) describe fixture harnesses and goldens under scripts/nemotron-qualification and state that tiny fixture passes do not qualify the shipping provider. That is appropriately cautious. One limit: the referenced scripts and README, docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md, and NEMOTRON_SUPER_REFERENCE_DIR handling are not in this diff. Any code or script that reads pinned reference directories, downloads checkpoints, or decodes images (Pillow, JPEG) would be new attack surface and needs review where it lands. No threat-model gaps follow from these doc-only changes.
